title: Quickstart
body:
Quickstart

Community scores for games, movies, TV series and books, from 0 to 10 in six categories per item, over a read-only JSON API.

1. Create an API key

Open your API dashboard and create a key. It starts with hx_live_ and is shown only once, so store it in an environment variable and never in client-side code.

The Free plan includes 100 requests in total, enough to build and test an integration.

2. Make your first request

The base URL is https://api.hexascore.app/v1. Every endpoint is a GET. Here are the five best-rated games:

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $HEXASCORE_API_KEY" \
  "https://api.hexascore.app/v1/games?sort=score&limit=5"

3. Read the response

Lists return data plus meta.next_cursor for the next page. Field names are snake_case and dates are ISO 8601. score and categories are null until an item has 5 ratings.

Next steps

  • Fetch one item with GET /v1/games/{id}.
  • Map ids you already have with GET /v1/lookup.
  • Handle errors and rate limits, then browse the API reference.

title: Authentication
body:
Authentication

Every request is authenticated with a secret API key sent as a Bearer token.

Bearer token

Send the key in the Authorization header. Keys look like hx_live_ followed by 32 letters and digits. Query-string keys are not accepted, so keys never end up in access logs or browser history.

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer hx_live_..." https://api.hexascore.app/v1/games

A missing, malformed, unknown or revoked key returns 401 with the unauthorized code and a WWW-Authenticate: Bearer header.

Managing keys

  • Create and revoke keys at /profile/api (verified email required, up to 5 active keys).
  • The full key is shown once. Only a SHA-256 hash is stored; we cannot recover it for you.
  • Revocation is immediate. Rotate by creating a new key, deploying it, then revoking the old one.
  • All keys of an account share the same plan, quota and per-second rate limit.

Keep keys secret

Call the API from your server. A key embedded in a web page or mobile app can be extracted and used to burn your quota. If a key leaks, revoke it right away.

title: Pagination
body:
Pagination

List endpoints use opaque cursors: stable under inserts, fast at any depth.

How it works

GET /v1/games, /v1/movies, /v1/series and /v1/books return { "data": [...], "meta": { "next_cursor": "..." } }. To get the next page, repeat the same request with cursor=<meta.next_cursor>. When meta.next_cursor is absent you reached the end.

  • Keep every other parameter identical. A cursor from another sort returns 400.
  • Cursors are opaque: do not parse or build them, their format may change.
  • Ordering is stable: ties are broken by item id, and unscored or undated items always come last.

Page size

limit defaults to 10. The maximum depends on your plan: 10 on Free, 100 on Pro and Business. A larger value returns 400 invalid-query; the API never silently truncates. Each page counts as one request.

Example: iterate over every page

let cursor = null;
do {
  const url = new URL("https://api.hexascore.app/v1/games");
  url.searchParams.set("limit", "100");
  if (cursor) url.searchParams.set("cursor", cursor);
  const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.HEXASCORE_API_KEY}` } });
  const page = await res.json();
  for (const game of page.data) console.log(game.title);
  cursor = page.meta.next_cursor ?? null;
} while (cursor);

Search

GET /v1/search is not paginated: it returns the best matches (up to 50) for a query, best first.

title: Rate limits
body:
Rate limits

Each plan has a request quota, a per-second rate limit and a maximum page size.

Plans

PlanQuotaRequests / secondMax page size
Free100 in total1 (burst of 5)10
Pro50,000 / month10100
Business500,000 / month50100

Prices and upgrades: /pricing.

What counts

  • Every authenticated request that reaches an endpoint counts as one, including 404s.
  • Not counted: 401, 400 for invalid parameters, 429 and any 5xx (refunded).
  • GET /v1/me/usage counts too, so read the response headers of your regular calls when you can.
  • Paid quotas reset at 00:00 UTC on the 1st of each month. The Free quota never resets.

Response headers

Successful responses tell you where you stand (IETF RateLimit header fields).

HeaderMeaning
RateLimit-LimitRequests in the current period (your plan quota).
RateLimit-RemainingRequests left before 402.
RateLimit-ResetSeconds until the quota resets; 0 for the lifetime Free quota.
Retry-AfterOn 429 and 503: seconds to wait before retrying.

When you hit a limit

The Free plan accepts a burst of 5 requests at once and then sustains 1 request per second; the other plans burst up to their per-second rate.

Too many requests per second returns 429 rate-limited: wait Retry-After seconds. Quota exhausted returns 402 quota-exhausted: upgrade your plan; retrying will not help until the reset.

title: Changes
body:
Changes

Poll one endpoint to keep your copy of the catalogue in sync, instead of crawling it again.

How it works

GET /v1/changes returns what changed since a point in time, oldest first. Each entry says which item changed, what happened to it and which fields moved, never the new values: refetch the item with GET /v1/{type}/{id} to read them. That way licence filtering and your plan's fields always apply to the data you read.

ParameterMeaning
sinceRequired. RFC 3339 timestamp, at most 14 days ago.
typeOptional. games, movies, series or books.
cursorOptional. The meta.next_cursor of the previous page.
limitOptional. 1 to 1000, default 100. This does not follow your plan's page size.

Each entry looks like this:

{
  "id": "chg_1048576",
  "action": "updated",
  "itemType": "games",
  "itemId": "0192f3a4-7b1c-7e21-9c55-3f1e2d4a6b71",
  "fields": ["score", "ratingCount"],
  "changedAt": "2026-11-02T10:14:12Z"
}
  • action is created, updated or deleted.
  • fields lists the API-visible field names that changed. Changes to hidden fields are not listed, and a score change is listed only when the one-decimal score, the confidence or ratingCount moved.
  • A merged duplicate is reported as deleted with mergedInto set to the id that replaces it.

Keep a copy in sync

Start with a since no older than 14 days, follow meta.next_cursor until it is empty, then store the changedAt of the last entry and use it as the next since. Entries are kept for 30 days but only the last 14 days can be queried; an older since returns changes-window-exceeded and a future one returns invalid-query. If you were offline for longer than 14 days, rebuild from the daily ID exports.

Every page counts as one request.

import { createHexascoreClient, getItem, listChanges } from "@hexascore/sdk";

const client = createHexascoreClient({ apiKey: process.env.HEXASCORE_API_KEY! });

let since = new Date(Date.now() - 24 * 3600 * 1000).toISOString();
let cursor: string | undefined;
do {
	const { data, error } = await listChanges({ client, query: { since, type: "games", limit: "500", cursor } });
	if (error) throw new Error(`${error.code}: ${error.detail}`);
	for (const change of data.data ?? []) {
		if (change.action === "deleted") continue; // drop the item, or follow mergedInto
		const item = await getItem({ client, path: { type: change.itemType, id: change.itemId } });
		// store item.data
		since = change.changedAt;
	}
	cursor = data.meta?.next_cursor || undefined;
} while (cursor);
import os
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

from hexascore import AuthenticatedClient
from hexascore.api.catalog import get_item, list_changes
from hexascore.models import Problem
from hexascore.types import UNSET

client = AuthenticatedClient(base_url="https://api.hexascore.app/v1", token=os.environ["HEXASCORE_API_KEY"])
since = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=1)).isoformat()

with client as c:
    cursor = UNSET
    while True:
        page = list_changes.sync(client=c, since=since, type_="games", limit="500", cursor=cursor)
        if isinstance(page, Problem) or page is None:
            raise RuntimeError(page.detail if page else "no response")
        for change in page.data:
            if change.action == "deleted":
                continue  # drop the item, or follow merged_into
            item = get_item.sync(change.item_type, client=c, id=change.item_id)
            since = change.changed_at
        cursor = page.meta.next_cursor
        if not cursor:
            break

Webhooks instead of polling

Pro and Business plans can have the same events pushed to a URL. See Webhooks. Webhook deliveries can be missed, so use /v1/changes to recover any gap.

title: Exports
body:
Exports

Download the whole list of item ids once a day, then fetch only what you need.

What is exported

Each day, before 08:00 UTC, we write one file per item type: games, movies, series and books. Files are kept for 90 days. Exports are available on the Pro and Business plans; the Free plan receives plan-required.

A file is gzip-compressed NDJSON, one JSON object per line:

{"id":"0192f3a4-7b1c-7e21-9c55-3f1e2d4a6b71","slug":"hades","wikidata":"Q62640075","updatedAt":"2026-11-02T06:12:44Z"}
FieldMeaning
idThe HexaScore item id, as used by GET /v1/{type}/{id}.
slugThe URL slug of the item page.
wikidataThe Wikidata entity id.
updatedAtWhen the item last changed.

The files carry ids only. Item data, scores and licence-restricted fields come from the regular endpoints, so the plan's rules always apply.

Download

GET /v1/exports lists the available files. GET /v1/exports/{type}/{day} (for example /v1/exports/games/2026-11-02) answers 302 to a download URL that is valid for 5 minutes. Follow the redirect straight away and do not store the URL.

curl -L -H "Authorization: Bearer $HEXASCORE_API_KEY" \
  "https://api.hexascore.app/v1/exports/games/2026-11-02" -o games_ids.json.gz
gunzip -c games_ids.json.gz | head -n 3

An unknown day, or one older than 90 days, returns not-found.

A good routine

  • Download the files once a day and compare with your copy: new ids are creations, missing ids are deletions.
  • Fetch the new ids with GET /v1/{type}/{id}, respecting your rate limits.
  • Between exports, follow Changes for the minute-by-minute view.

title: Webhooks
body:
Webhooks

Get a signed HTTP request when items change, instead of polling.

Set up

Webhooks are available on the Pro (2 endpoints) and Business (10 endpoints) plans. Create an endpoint with POST /v1/webhooks:

FieldMeaning
urlAn https URL that answers within a few seconds. Private and internal addresses are refused.
eventsOne or more of item.created, item.updated, item.deleted.
itemTypesOne or more of games, movies, series, books.

The response contains the signing secret, which starts with whsec_. It is shown once: store it in your secrets manager. Use GET /v1/webhooks to list endpoints, DELETE /v1/webhooks/{id} to remove one and POST /v1/webhooks/{id}/test to send a test delivery. Managing webhooks does not count against your quota.

What we send

We send a batch of up to 100 events as one POST with a JSON body. Payloads carry ids and field names only; refetch the item to read its data.

{
  "type": "item.batch",
  "deliveredAt": "2026-11-02T10:15:00Z",
  "events": [
    {
      "id": "chg_1048576",
      "type": "item.updated",
      "itemType": "games",
      "itemId": "0192f3a4-7b1c-7e21-9c55-3f1e2d4a6b71",
      "fields": ["score", "ratingCount"],
      "changedAt": "2026-11-02T10:14:12Z"
    },
    {
      "id": "chg_1048577",
      "type": "item.deleted",
      "itemType": "movies",
      "itemId": "0192f3a4-7b1c-7e21-9c55-3f1e2d4a5521",
      "mergedInto": "0192f3a4-7b1c-7e21-9c55-3f1e2d4a5520",
      "changedAt": "2026-11-02T10:14:30Z"
    }
  ]
}

Events for the same item inside one delivery window are coalesced. Event ids are unique, so use them to ignore a repeat.

Verify the signature

Deliveries follow the Standard Webhooks scheme. Every request has three headers: webhook-id, webhook-timestamp (Unix seconds) and webhook-signature (one or more space-separated v1,<base64> values).

To verify a delivery:

  • Read the raw request body. Do not parse and re-serialise it.
  • Reject the request when webhook-timestamp is more than 5 minutes from your clock.
  • Compute the base64 HMAC-SHA256 of <webhook-id>.<webhook-timestamp>.<raw body>, using the secret without its whsec_ prefix, base64-decoded, as the key.
  • Compare it with each v1 value in constant time. Accept the request when one matches.
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";

export function verifyWebhook(secret: string, headers: Headers, rawBody: string): boolean {
	const id = headers.get("webhook-id");
	const timestamp = headers.get("webhook-timestamp");
	const signatures = headers.get("webhook-signature");
	if (!id || !timestamp || !signatures) return false;
	if (Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - Number(timestamp)) > 300) return false;

	const key = Buffer.from(secret.replace(/^whsec_/, ""), "base64");
	const expected = createHmac("sha256", key).update(`${id}.${timestamp}.${rawBody}`).digest();
	return signatures.split(" ").some((entry) => {
		const [version, value] = entry.split(",");
		if (version !== "v1" || !value) return false;
		const got = Buffer.from(value, "base64");
		return got.length === expected.length && timingSafeEqual(got, expected);
	});
}
import base64
import binascii
import hashlib
import hmac
import time


def verify_webhook(secret: str, headers: dict[str, str], raw_body: bytes) -> bool:
    try:
        msg_id = headers["webhook-id"]
        timestamp = headers["webhook-timestamp"]
        signatures = headers["webhook-signature"]
        if abs(time.time() - int(timestamp)) > 300:
            return False
    except (KeyError, ValueError):
        return False

    key = base64.b64decode(secret.removeprefix("whsec_"))
    signed = f"{msg_id}.{timestamp}.".encode() + raw_body
    expected = hmac.new(key, signed, hashlib.sha256).digest()
    for entry in signatures.split(" "):
        version, _, value = entry.partition(",")
        try:
            got = base64.b64decode(value)
        except binascii.Error:
            continue
        if version == "v1" and hmac.compare_digest(got, expected):
            return True
    return False

Retries and failures

Answer with any 2xx status within a few seconds, and do the real work afterwards. We retry other answers and timeouts 8 times with growing delays, starting at 30 seconds. A 410 Gone stops the delivery for good. After three deliveries in a row run out of retries, the endpoint is disabled and we email the account owner. Deliveries are logged for 30 days.

Delivery is at least once and not strictly ordered. Webhooks can still miss events, so call /v1/changes with the since of your last processed event to fill any gap.

title: Errors
body:
Errors

Errors use RFC 9457 problem details with a stable machine-readable code.

Format

Every error has Content-Type: application/problem+json. Branch on code (stable) rather than on title or detail (human text that may change). type links to the matching section below, and request_id equals the X-Request-Id header: include it when you contact support.

{
  "type": "https://hexascore.app/problems/quota-exhausted",
  "title": "Quota exhausted",
  "status": 402,
  "detail": "Monthly quota is exhausted. Upgrade at https://hexascore.app/pricing.",
  "instance": "/api/v1/games",
  "request_id": "01JB7Q4V0Q8M3K2Y7T9H5N6C1D",
  "code": "quota-exhausted",
  "plan": "pro",
  "limit": 50000
}

Codes

invalid-query

HTTP 400. A query parameter is unknown or out of range, or limit is above your plan's page size (10 on Free). errors lists each problem with its path. Fix the listed parameters. Not counted against your quota.

invalid-cursor

HTTP 400. The cursor was tampered with or belongs to another query. Restart from the first page.

changes-window-exceeded

HTTP 400. The since window of /v1/changes is larger than the endpoint allows. Request a more recent since.

unauthorized

HTTP 401. No Authorization: Bearer header, a malformed key, or a key that does not exist or was revoked. Check the header and the key at /profile/api. Never retried automatically.

quota-exhausted

HTTP 402. The 100 lifetime requests on Free, or the monthly quota on paid plans. The body includes plan and limit. Upgrade your plan at /pricing. Paid quotas reset on the 1st of each month (UTC).

plan-required

HTTP 403. The endpoint needs a higher plan. Upgrade at /pricing.

account-banned

HTTP 403. The account that owns the key is suspended. Contact us through /contact with the request_id.

not-found

HTTP 404. Unknown item id, an id that belongs to another type (for example a game id under /movies), an unknown type path, or no match for /lookup. Lookups require an exact id.

rate-limited

HTTP 429. More requests per second than your plan allows. The Retry-After header says how many seconds to wait. Not counted against your quota. Space out bursts or upgrade for a higher rate.

internal-error

HTTP 500. Something failed on our side. The request is refunded to your quota. Retry with exponential backoff; if it persists, send us the request_id.

community-submissions-closed

HTTP 403. Community suggestions are switched off right now. Try again later.

suggestion-not-eligible

HTTP 403. Your account cannot submit suggestions (unverified email, too new, banned from submissions, or the suggestion is not yours).

suggestion-duplicate

HTTP 409. An open suggestion for the same item and fields already exists. Edit or withdraw it instead.

stale-before

HTTP 409. The field changed since you loaded it. Reload and re-apply your edit.

invalid-transition

HTTP 409. The suggestion cannot move from its current status to the requested one.

field-locked

HTTP 423. A moderator locked this field; community edits to it are not accepted.

suggestion-quota

HTTP 429. You reached your daily suggestion quota. Try again after the reset.

suggestion-cooldown

HTTP 429. Wait for the cooldown to pass; the Retry-After header gives the seconds.

validation

HTTP 422. The submission failed validation.

service-unavailable

HTTP 503. A dependency is temporarily down. Comes with Retry-After. Retry after the indicated delay.

Retries

Retry only 429, 500 and 503, honouring Retry-After when present and backing off exponentially otherwise. Every endpoint is a read-only GET, so retries are always safe.

title: Data coverage
body:
Data coverage

Every field the API returns comes from a source we are allowed to republish. Some fields are therefore patchy, and some are always omitted. This page states what to expect before you build on it.

Fields and their sources

FieldSourceExpected gap
id, type, slug, url, score fields, trending, timeToBeatHexaScore (API terms)none
title, releaseDate, genres, people, organisations, franchises, platforms, countries, runtime, pages, seasons, episodesWikidata (CC0) and the communityruntime, platforms and episode counts are patchy
synopsisWikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0, with sourceUrl)items without an article
editions and book coversOpen Library and Wikidatanot applicable to other types
covers for films, series and games, and trailersnonenever in the API
externalIdsWikidata, ISBN-13, Open LibraryTMDB, IGDB and Steam ids are omitted

Every response lists the fields it left out in meta.omittedFields, and each sourced value carries its provenance (source and licence).

Coverage percentages

The table below gives, per type, the share of public items for which the API returns each field. It is measured with qa/sql/api_coverage.sql on a copy of the production catalogue, using the same source rules as the API, and shows the date of the measurement.

title: Changelog
body:
Changelog

The version is part of the path. v1 only changes in backwards-compatible ways.

Versioning policy

Within /v1 we only make additive changes: new endpoints, new optional parameters, new response fields and new error detail texts. Ignore unknown fields and do not rely on field order.

Breaking changes (removing or renaming a field, changing a type, making a parameter required) ship as a new path (/v2). Error code values, category keys and sort names are part of the contract.

Deprecation and sunset

  • A deprecated version keeps working for at least 6 months after its successor is released.
  • Its responses carry Deprecation (RFC 9745) and Sunset (RFC 8594) headers with the date it stops working, plus a Link to this page.
  • Account owners with recent traffic on the old version are emailed at deprecation and 30 days before sunset.

Changes

v1: first release

  • Lists, details and genres for games, movies, series and books.
  • /search, /lookup by external id and /me/usage.
